BACKGROUND. `drain_condition_heldout.py` builds a held-out set (drawer, truck, passenger seat, laptop narrations, some authored edits) so a person can label each row forbidden or clean: forbidden means the narration states, as fact, that the thing is open/ajar/lifted/entered or states what is inside it, beyond what the world declares AFTER the engine acted on that turn. A previous step added `declared_state` (state before the turn) to 40 of 49 rows. That is still not enough to label: the label also depends on (1) the player's command and (2) whether the ENGINE itself opened the thing during that turn (a drawer the engine opened may be described open). Two more problems: the blind sheet masks thing names by replacing them with 'the object', which garbles text ('the the object'), and the sheet does not show the command.

TASK. (1) For every real row take, from the recorded turn it came from (enforce rows carry `input`, `engine_opened`, `focus_open_state_after`, `focus_open_state_committed`; read the recorded fields, never infer them from prose): `command` (the player's input), `engine_opened` (bool), `open_state_after` (the recorded open/closed state after the turn, or null if the thing declares none). Rows from files that do not record these (the defect-probe files) get `labelable: false` and a `labelable_missing_reason`; rows with a declared_state AND command AND engine_opened get `labelable: true`. Authored rows inherit all of these from their source row. (2) Fix the masking: render the thing's name as the bracketed token `[thing]` (replace the whole name where it occurs, keep the article before it as is) so text reads `the [thing]`, not `the the object`, and mask the name inside the command too. Do the masking deterministically from the row's `thing` field and its package aliases; this is blinding only, never a decision input. (3) The blind sheet prints, under each narration, `Command: ...` and `Declared: ...` (the declared state before, plus whether the engine opened it this turn and the state after), in neutral words with no source file and no label word, and lists only labelable rows (a separate file `unlabelable.json` lists the rest with reasons). Keep shuffling with a fixed seed and every existing mode and field working. At least 30 rows must be labelable; report the count per thing and the reason for each unlabelable row in your summary.

TESTS: update tests/test_drain_condition_heldout.py for command/engine_opened/open_state_after on a fixture row, an unlabelable row with a reason, authored inheritance, the `[thing]` masking (no doubled article, no leak of the real name), and the sheet's Command and Declared lines.
